Title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Abstract/intro framing: benchmark tests whether user-disclosed secrets remain recoverable after unrelated conversational topic drift and persuasion/probing, focusing on active-context behavioral privacy risk rather than training-data memorization or immediate jailbreaks. Users need not believe literal forgetting; risk is underestimating elicitation later through indirect/justified/high-pressure/tool-mediated prompts in shared sessions, browser assistants, enterprise copilots, agentic workflows, prompt injection.

final_notes:
Title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Focus: active-context/inference-time re-disclosure after topic drift, not training memorization, personalization/cross-session memory, unlearning/static privacy reasoning/jailbreaks. Threat model: user discloses secret S at t0; after d unrelated drift turns, standardized probe P appended; leakage if response reveals S exactly/approximately/semantically.

Benchmark: 1,000 controlled dialogues total per model (900 synthetic + 100 human-authored), same 1,000 evaluated on each of 3 models and 3 probes = 3,000 cached responses/model, 9,000 total. Human dialogues inserted throughout, not separately identifiable; no human-vs-synthetic analysis. Models: GPT-OSS-120B, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3-VL-235B via OpenRouter/API. One seeded secret/dialogue; d∈{0,2,3,4,5,6}; short-to-medium drift only. Secret categories: SSN, credit card, email, phone; unstructured left future. Probes: Simple, Medium, Hard.

Appendix A dataset by drift: d0 N=197 avg words/tokens 44.29/59.05; d2 N=147 253.97/338.62; d3 N=142 344.18/458.91; d4 N=166 452.27/603.02; d5 N=181 520.92/694.56; d6 N=167 568.03/757.37. Counts sum 1,000. Tokens estimated from word counts.

Detector: regex/normalization first, fuzzy matching, Llama judge for regex-negative; dialogue leak if any probe leaks. Stats: bootstrap CIs, McNemar+Bonferroni, Cochran Q, chi-square+Cramer’s V. τ uses δ=0.1*L(0), sustained below threshold else max(Dobs)+1.

Results: hybrid dialogue leakage GPT 47.70, DeepSeek 38.70, Qwen 54.60. Drift does not reliably reduce leakage; τ=7 for all models/persuasion levels, exceeding observed max d=6. Secret type strongest association; emails/phones high, SSN/cards low. Appendix B probe-level Cramer’s V: secret type large (DeepSeek .5871, GPT .7731, Qwen .6927); drift small/negligible (.1073/.0659/.0723); persuasion negligible (.0718/.0689/.0639).

Threat model: user discloses secret S at t0; after d unrelated, content-dense drift turns, standardized probe P appended; leakage if response reveals S exactly, approximately, or semantically. Practical risks: shared/persistent sessions, enterprise copilots/agents, tool outputs/retrieved docs/prompt injection, browser/app assistants.

Benchmark/eval: Introduction said 1,000 dialogues per model; §3 says N=1000 controlled dialogues total benchmark, 900 synthetic + 100 human-authored interspersed; no human-vs-synthetic comparison due to missing identifiers. Three LLMs with extended context windows. Dataset summary: secret categories=4; drift lengths 0,2,3,4,5,6; avg words 359.16, median 385, min/max 43/795; avg approx tokens 478.87, median 513.33, min/max 57.33/1060.00. §3.2.1 lists four fixed-format PII categories: phone numbers, email addresses, SSNs, credit cards. Earlier intro notes had included health-related details too—possible inconsistency.

Generation: scaffold-then-rewrite; personas from >100 professions/demographics; secret inserted in opening turn for plausible task. Drift topics include tax filing, medical triage, travel logistics; dense QA/fallback tasks; some human-authored drift turns in library. Rewriting model improves fluency/persona realism while preserving exact secret, drift length, role structure, final probe conditions.

Probes: Simple direct neutral; Medium justified/contextual; Hard high-pressure/urgent. Drift distribution: d=0 with p=.2; otherwise uniform over {2,3,4,5,6} with p=.8. Main reported leakage from earlier: dialogue-level hybrid 38.7%–54.6%; SSNs/credit cards suppressed more than emails/phones; extra drift up to 6 doesn’t reliably reduce leakage; Privacy Half-Life τ no stable decay observed.

Title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Focus: active-context/inference-time re-disclosure, not training-data memorization/unlearning/static privacy reasoning/jailbreaks. Threat model: user discloses secret S at t0; after d unrelated drift turns, standardized probe P appended; leakage if response reveals S exactly/approximately/semantically.

Benchmark: 1,000 controlled dialogues total (900 synthetic + 100 human-authored), same 1,000 evaluated on each of 3 models and 3 probes = 3,000 cached responses/model, 9,000 total. Models: GPT-OSS-120B, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3-VL-235B via OpenRouter. One seeded secret/dialogue; d∈{0,2,3,4,5,6}; d=0 p=.2, others uniform. Secret categories in §3/results: phone, email, SSN, credit card; intro earlier mentioned health-related details too (possible inconsistency if later treated as benchmark category). Probes: Simple, Medium, Hard.

Detector: regex/normalization first, Llama judge for regex-negative; dialogue leak if any probe leaks; probe-level for persuasion/fuzzy. Stats: bootstrap CIs, McNemar+Bonferroni, Cochran Q, chi-square+Cramer’s V. Privacy Half-Life τ uses δ=0.1*L(0), sustained below threshold else max(Dobs)+1.

Results §5: Dialogue-level hybrid vs regex: GPT 47.70 vs 47.70 (+0, p=1); DeepSeek 38.70 vs 37.80 (+0.90, p=7.7e-3); Qwen 54.60 vs 53.50 (+1.10, p=2.57e-3). Hybrid dialogue leakage CIs: DeepSeek 38.70 [35.7,41.6], GPT 47.70 [44.6,50.8], Qwen 54.60 [51.6,57.7]. Probe leakage by persuasion: GPT S39.30/M40.50/H32.90; DeepSeek 28.10/22.00/29.20; Qwen 38.70/33.30/40.60. Drift effect small; dip near d=3 rebound. Secret type strong: emails/phones high, SSN/credit cards low. τ=7 for all models/persuasion levels. Fuzzy 0.85 close to probe hybrid.

Summary claims: Paper studies whether secrets disclosed in active LLM conversation remain recoverable after unrelated topic shifts. Benchmark PrivDrift: 1,000 controlled dialogues with seeded secrets, unrelated intervening turns, standardized extraction probes. Three models tested with direct, justified, and high-pressure probes. Paper studies active-context privacy: whether user-disclosed structured secrets remain recoverable after unrelated topic drift. PrivDrift benchmark: 1,000 controlled/synthetic dialogues with seeded ground-truth secret S, unrelated content-dense drift turns, then standardized probes P. Drift length d = number of turns between disclosure and final probe; sampled from Uniform{2,3,4,5,6}. Active context means current conversation/context window, not model parameters or cross-session memory. Secret categories include SSN plus emails, phone numbers, credit cards (from earlier summary). Three target models via OpenRouter: GPT-OSS-120B (GPT-OSS), DeepSeek-R1 (DeepSeek), Qwen3-VL-235B (Qwen). Persuasion/probe levels: Simple/direct neutral, Medium/contextual justification, Hard/high-pressure/urgent. Leakage event = response reveals exact, approximate, or semantic secret. Dialogue-level leakage = any standardized probe elicits secret in a dialogue; probe-level = individual response leakage. Hybrid detector: normalization/regex containment of normalized secret in normalized response, then for negatives an open-weights Llama LLM judge; fuzzy matching is auxiliary. Dialogue-level leakage reported earlier ranges 38.7%–54.6%; persuasion effects model-dependent; SSNs/credit cards suppressed more often than emails/phones; for d≤6, more drift does not reliably reduce leakage; no model reaches stable suppression criterion. Privacy Half-Life τ = earliest observed drift length below safety threshold δ=0.1×L(0) with no later observed resurgence, using observed drift set D_obs. Statistics: 95% bootstrap CIs over dialogues; McNemar for paired detector/model comparisons (Bonferroni where applicable), Cochran’s Q across persuasion levels, chi-square independence and Cramer’s V for associations. Related contrasts: not training-data memorization, membership inference, immediate jailbreaks, prompt injection, or parameter-level unlearning; focuses on information-flow control for active-context re-disclosure.

Paper topic: whether unrelated conversational tasks prevent later disclosure of sensitive information already present in an active LLM conversation. PrivDrift setup: seeded multi-turn histories, content-dense intervening exchanges, three standardized extraction conditions. Dataset: 1,000 dialogues containing one of four secret types: phone numbers, email addresses, Social Security Numbers, or credit card numbers. Findings claimed: leakage varies by model, secret type, and persuasion intensity; SSNs and credit card numbers are much more strongly suppressed than contact identifiers; no system achieves stable suppression within tested drift lengths. Framing/caveat: active-context behavioral privacy failure, not evidence of permanent memory.

Paper title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Active-context privacy: same-session/persistent shared/tool-augmented LLMs can re-disclose user secrets after unrelated tasks; not parameter memorization/immediate jailbreak. Dataset: 1000 dialogues, 900 synthetic/100 human; secret types A2L phone, F8Z email, W3B SSN, N6G credit card. D7A values {0,2,3,4,5,6}; probe styles C8R simple, Z2F contextual, L9W urgent. H8D detector positive if deterministic normalized inclusion U3P/B6T or Llama judge finds identifying disclosure. K2V tau = first d with L(d)<=0.1L(0) and all later; empty=>max(Dobs)+1.

Experimental setup: full QX2 standardized, 3000 cached responses/model, 9000 total = 3 models x 1000 dialogues x 3 probes. Models: M7Q=GPT-OSS-120B, T4X=DeepSeek-R1, Y9C=Qwen3-VL-235B. G4P=any-probe dialogue leakage; P6S=probe-level.

Results: H8D G4P: T4X 38.70 [35.7,41.6], M7Q 47.70 [44.6,50.8], Y9C 54.60 [51.6,57.7]. P6S by V4N: M7Q C8R 39.30/Z2F 40.50/L9W 32.90; T4X 28.10/22.00/29.20; Y9C 38.70/33.30/40.60; text earlier incorrectly said T4X maximizes at Z2F. D7A associations small/negligible; dip near d=3 then rebound; K2V=7 for all. S8Q strongly determines leakage; W3B/N6G much lower than F8Z/A2L; conclusion says S8Q asymmetry suggests safeguards depend on format/sensitivity cues rather than generalized contextual confidentiality/reasoning. Cached Table6 P6S H8D: T4X 26.43, M7Q 37.57, Y9C 37.53; R5J 0.85 closely tracks.

Limitations: D7A bounded short/medium not full-window; fixed-format only; no cross-session/training/personalization memory; human-vs-synthetic comparison deferred; no formal human-auto IAA; API models may change; planned artifacts aggregate/sanitized with non-real identifiers.

Appendix A D7A counts/lengths: d0 N197 avg 44 words/59 tokens; d2 N147 254/339; d3 N142 344/459; d4 N166 452/603; d5 N181 521/695; d6 N167 568/757; total 1000. Title/scope: PrivDrift audits active-context re-disclosure after unrelated topic drift + standardized probes; excludes transcript access, training memorization, unlearning, immediate jailbreaks, cross-session memory. Dataset: 1,000 dialogues/model for 3 models; 3 probes/dialogue => 3,000 cached responses/model, 9,000 total. 900 synthetic + 100 human-authored; cached metadata lacks human/synthetic row labels, so no human-vs-synthetic comparison. Secret categories: phone, email, SSN, credit card; fixed-format only. Dobs={0,2,3,4,5,6}; p=.2 d=0, p=.8 uniform 2..6; bounded drift up to d=6. Overall avg words 359.16; avg tokens 478.87. Appendix Table 7 drift counts/lengths: d0 N=197 avg words/tokens 44.29/59.05; d2 N=147 253.97/338.62; d3 N=142 344.18/458.91; d4 N=166 452.27/603.02; d5 N=181 520.92/694.56; d6 N=167 568.03/757.37; total N=1000, weighted averages match overall.
Probes: Simple, Medium, Hard. Detection: regex normalization then Llama judge for regex-negatives; fuzzy also reported; dialogue-level leak if any probe leaks.
Sec5 results: Dialogue-level regex/hybrid: GPT 47.70/47.70, DeepSeek 37.80/38.70, Qwen 53.50/54.60; hybrid range 38.7–54.6. Hybrid CIs: DeepSeek [35.7,41.6], GPT [44.6,50.8], Qwen [51.6,57.7]. Appendix B Table 8 repeats these as probe-level effect sizes. Half-life τ=7 censoring/exceeds observed d≤6; dips not stable enough.

Study: active-context privacy; seeded secret S at t0 remains in context, then d unrelated drift turns, then probes; leakage if response reveals S exactly/approximately/semantically. Threat is model re-disclosure, not transcript access. Dataset N=1,000 (900 synthetic/100 human); no human-vs-synthetic comparison because cached metadata lacks human-authored rows. Dialogue leakage=any of 3 probes leaks; persuasion/fuzzy probe-level.

Detector: Stage 1 normalized containment; Stage 2 Llama judge only for regex-negative. Fuzzy matching also. No formal human–automated inter-annotator agreement; future manual audit planned. Dialogue rates use bootstrap CIs; tests include McNemar, Cochran Q, chi-square/Cramer’s V. Privacy Half-Life tau=min observed d where L(d)<=0.1*L(0) and all later observed also; if none tau=7.

Table 4 persuasion probe-level: GPT Simple 39.30, Medium 40.50, Hard 32.90; DeepSeek 28.10,22.00,29.20; Qwen 38.70,33.30,40.60. Drift dip near d=3 then rebound. Table 5: SSN GPT/DeepSeek/Qwen 0.14/1.11/5.97; credit card 0.00/0.39/4.01; email 78.24/57.11/81.13; phone 70.89/46.13/57.24. Half-life tau=7 all models/persuasion (d≤6). Table 6 fuzzy ≈ hybrid. Appendix B/Table 8 effect sizes: secret type large V DeepSeek .5871, GPT .7731, Qwen .6927; drift DeepSeek small .1073, GPT negligible .0659, Qwen negligible .0723; persuasion negligible .0718/.0689/.0639. Conclusion: persistent substantial leakage, strongest secret-type asymmetry, no stable decay. Limitations: bounded d≤6; structured secrets only; active context not memory/training/cross-session; API models may change; planned sanitized artifact release.

Formal setup: secret S disclosed at t0; d unrelated content-dense drift turns D={u1,a1,...,ud,ad}; standardized probe P appended; leakage if response reveals S exactly, approximately, or semantically. Dataset: N=1000 controlled dialogues; 900 synthetic + 100 human-authored inserted throughout; metadata lacks human-authored identifiers so only aggregate results, no human-vs-synthetic comparison. Table 1: 4 secret categories; drift lengths 0,2,3,4,5,6; avg/median words 359.16/385; min/max words 43/795; avg/median approx tokens 478.87/513.33; min/max tokens 57.33/1060. Secret categories: phone numbers, emails, SSNs, credit cards; inserted in opening turn with persona from >100 profiles. Drift topics include tax filing, medical triage, travel logistics; drift turns from dense topic-conditioned Q&A/fallback professional writing, reasoning, summarization; subset human-authored. Naturalistic refinement preserves exact secret, drift length, role structure, final probe conditions. Probes: Simple/direct neutral; Medium/contextual justification; Hard/high-pressure/urgent. Drift sampling: d=0 p=.2; otherwise uniform over {2,3,4,5,6} p=.8. Evaluated across three extended-context LLMs with 1,000 dialogues/model. Evaluation: hierarchical hybrid detector; Stage 1 normalization matching: numeric strip non-digits; alphanumeric normalize case/whitespace preserving delimiters; regex leak if phi(S) subset phi(R). Stage 2: regex-negative responses go to open-weights Llama judge with secret+response; judge flags full secret, substantial substring/partial identifying info, indirect hints/format variations. Regex-only and hybrid rates reported separately. Privacy Half-Life tau: threshold delta=0.1*L(0); min observed d with L(d)<=delta and all later observed d’ also <=delta; if none, tau=max(Dobs)+1; prevents transient dips. Main results noted earlier: hybrid leakage 38.7–54.6%, SSNs/credit cards suppressed less than emails/phones, d≤6 does not reliably reduce leakage, no model reaches stable privacy half-life decay.

Title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” PrivDrift measures active-context re-disclosure: whether a model reproduces a user-disclosed secret later after unrelated topic drift/probes, not transcript presence, training memorization, unlearning, jailbreaks, unsafe generation, or instruction hijacking. Formal setup: secret S at t0; d unrelated drift turns D; standardized probe P; leakage if response reveals S exactly/approximately/semantically. Dataset: 1,000 dialogues (900 synthetic + 100 human-authored inserted throughout; metadata lacks human identifiers, so aggregate only); one seeded secret; drift lengths {0,2,3,4,5,6} with d=0 p=.2, otherwise uniform p=.8. Secret types: phone, email, SSN, credit card. Table 1: avg/median words 359.16/385; min/max words 43/795; avg/median approx tokens 478.87/513.33; min/max tokens 57.33/1060. Probes: Simple/direct neutral; Medium/contextual justification; Hard/high-pressure urgent. Models: GPT-OSS-120B, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3-VL-235B via OpenRouter; same histories/templates. Detection: regex-only plus hybrid hierarchical detector: Stage 1 normalization/regex; Stage 2 regex-negative Llama judge flags full, substantial partial identifying info, or indirect hints/format variations. Summary claims: Paper studies whether secrets disclosed in active LLM conversations remain recoverable after unrelated topic shifts. Benchmark PrivDrift has 1,000 controlled dialogues with seeded secrets, unrelated intervening turns, standardized extraction probes. Three models tested with direct, justified, and high-pressure probes. Hybrid detector = normalized matching + LLM judge. Dialogue-level leakage defined as whether any standardized probe elicits the secret; reported range 38.7% to 54.6%. Persuasion effects depend on model. Paper studies active-context privacy: whether seeded secrets disclosed in ongoing LLM conversations remain recoverable after unrelated topic drift. PrivDrift benchmark: 1,000 controlled dialogues built via parametric scaffold-then-rewrite pipeline; includes personas, four PII secret categories (SSN, credit card, email, phone), content-dense unrelated drift turns, and standardized probes. Drift length d = number of turns between secret disclosure and final probe; sampled includes d<=6. Models evaluated via OpenRouter: GPT-OSS-120B (GPT-OSS), DeepSeek-R1 (DeepSeek), Qwen3-VL-235B (Qwen). Persuasion levels: Simple/direct neutral, Medium/contextual justification, Hard/high-pressure urgent. Probe-level leakage = individual response reveals secret; dialogue-level leakage = any standardized probe elicits secret in a dialogue. Leakage event includes exact, approximate, or semantic revelation. Hybrid detector = normalization/regex containment of normalized secret in response, then Llama LLM judge for regex-negative responses; fuzzy matching auxiliary. Reported summary claims to check: dialogue-level leakage range 38.7%–54.6%; persuasion effects depend on model; SSNs and credit cards suppressed more than emails/phones; more drift within d<=6 does not reliably reduce leakage; no model achieves stable suppression. Privacy Half-Life tau = earliest observed drift length with L(d) below safety threshold delta=0.1*L(0) and no later resurgence. Stats mentioned: 95% bootstrap CIs over dialogues, McNemar paired tests with Bonferroni where applicable, Cochran’s Q across persuasion, chi-square independence and Cramer’s V.

Paper topic: PrivDrift/QX2 audits active-context re-disclosure of user-supplied secrets after unrelated conversation; not parameter memorization/static privacy norms/jailbreaks/unlearning/cross-session retention. Dataset N=1,000 dialogues; 900 synthetic + 100 human-authored, but §7 says cached metadata no longer preserves human-authored row identifiers, so separate human-vs-synthetic comparisons deferred/only aggregate results. Secret types S8Q: A2L phone, F8Z email, W3B SSN, N6G credit card; fixed-format only. D7A values {0,2,3,4,5,6}; §3.3 says d=0 p=.2 and Uniform{2..6} p=.8. Appendix A Table7 counts by d: 0=197, 2=147, 3=142, 4=166, 5=181, 6=167 (sum 1000). Probes V4N: C8R neutral, Z2F contextual justification, L9W urgent. Detection H8D: deterministic normalized matching plus Llama judge on negatives; deterministic baseline called B6T/U3P/R5J inconsistently. G4P dialogue-level positive if any standardized probe leaks; P6S probe-level. τ: δ=0.1*L(0); if none τ=max(Dobs)+1.
Models: M7Q GPT-OSS-120B, T4X DeepSeek-R1, Y9C Qwen3-VL-235B via OpenRouter/API; 3,000 cached responses/model; §7 cautions API identities may change.
Results: Table2 G4P U3P vs H8D: M7Q 47.70/47.70 Δ0 p1; T4X 37.80/38.70 Δ.90 p7.7e-3; Y9C 53.50/54.60 Δ1.10 p2.57e-3. Table3 H8D G4P: T4X 38.70, M7Q 47.70, Y9C 54.60. Table4 P6S by V4N: M7Q 39.30/40.50/32.90; T4X 28.10/22.00/29.20; Y9C 38.70/33.30/40.60. Table5: W3B/N6G low vs F8Z/A2L high; no stable suppression through d<=6; τ=7 every model/condition. Table6 cached P6S: H8D T4X26.43 M7Q37.57 Y9C37.53; R5J close. Appendix B Table8 effect sizes: S8Q large for all (T4X .5871, M7Q .7731, Y9C .6927); D7A small/negligible (.1073/.0659/.0723); V4N negligible (.0718/.0689/.0639). Conclusion: secret-type asymmetry suggests format-sensitive safeguards, not generalized contextual confidentiality.

final_notes:
Conclusion: PrivDrift audits active-context privacy leakage under topic drift and persuasion. Across 3 LLMs and 1,000 dialogues/model, dialogue-level hybrid leakage: DeepSeek 38.70%, GPT 47.70%, Qwen 54.60%.

Regex vs hybrid: GPT 47.70 vs 47.70 (+0, p=1.0); DeepSeek 37.80 vs 38.70 (+0.90, p=7.7e-3); Qwen 53.50 vs 54.60 (+1.10, p=2.57e-3). Hybrid CIs: DeepSeek [35.7,41.6], GPT [44.6,50.8], Qwen [51.6,57.7]. Hybrid adds only up to 1.10 pp; leakage mostly direct/near-direct; fuzzy tracks hybrid.

Probe-level hybrid by persuasion: GPT Simple 39.30, Medium 40.50, Hard 32.90; DeepSeek 28.10, 22.00, 29.20; Qwen 38.70, 33.30, 40.60. Cochran Q p<1e-5 all; non-monotonic/model-dependent. Appendix B persuasion effect sizes: DeepSeek V=0.0718, GPT V=0.0689, Qwen V=0.0639, all negligible.

Drift: curves dip near d=3 then rebound; small/negligible effects: Cramer’s V DeepSeek 0.1073 small, GPT 0.0659 negligible, Qwen 0.0723 negligible. Risk persists through d≤6; not long-context.

Secret type probe-level hybrid: GPT SSN 0.14, card 0.00, email 78.24, phone 70.89; DeepSeek SSN 1.11, card 0.39, email 57.11, phone 46.13; Qwen SSN 5.97, card 4.01, email 81.13, phone 57.24. Appendix B secret-type effect sizes: DeepSeek V=0.5871, GPT V=0.7731, Qwen V=0.6927, all large.

Privacy Half-Life: δ=0.1·L(0), none reaches threshold; τ=7, exceeding observed d≤6, for all models/persuasion levels.

Limitations: fixed-format secrets; active context not training/cross-session; 900 synthetic+100 human-authored but metadata can’t identify human rows; surface detectors; no formal human IAA; API logged/cached.

Appendix A Table 7 dataset lengths by drift: d=0 N197 avg words/tokens 44.29/59.05; d=2 N147 253.97/338.62; d=3 N142 344.18/458.91; d=4 N166 452.27/603.02; d=5 N181 520.92/694.56; d=6 N167 568.03/757.37. N sums to 1000. Appendix C only says Figure 6 dialogue construction details.

Paper title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Abstract claims PrivDrift is a benchmark for whether user-disclosed secrets remain recoverable after conversational topic drift and persuasion-based probing. Dataset: 1,000 controlled multi-turn dialogues with seeded secrets, content-dense drift turns, standardized extraction probes. Evaluation: three LLMs with extended context windows. Main reported result: dialogue-level hybrid leakage ranges from 38.7% to 54.6%, varying strongly by model, secret type, and persuasion intensity. Claim: within tested drift window, additional topic drift does not reliably reduce leakage. Framing: privacy risk in active LLM contexts should be evaluated as persistent behavioral failure mode, not only training-data memorization or immediate jailbreak behavior.

Title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Abstract/intro framing: benchmark tests whether user-disclosed secrets remain recoverable after unrelated conversational topic drift and persuasion/probing, focusing on active-context behavioral privacy risk rather than training-data memorization or immediate jailbreaks. Users need not believe literal forgetting; risk is underestimating elicitation later through indirect/justified/high-pressure/tool-mediated prompts in shared sessions, browser assistants, enterprise copilots, agentic workflows, prompt injection.

Dataset/eval: PrivDrift uses controlled multi-turn dialogues with seeded secrets, content-dense unrelated drift turns, standardized extraction probes. Abstract said 1,000 controlled dialogues; intro says across three LLMs with extended context windows and “1,000 dialogues per model” (could mean same 1,000 evaluated on each model). Axes: topic drift = number of unrelated turns between secret disclosure and probing; persuasion intensity = interaction style. Tested drift window d ≤ 6.

Reported results so far: dialogue-level hybrid leakage ranges 38.7%–54.6%, substantial across models. Persuasion intensity significantly affects leakage. Leakage varies sharply by secret type: SSNs and credit cards suppressed more often than emails and phone numbers. Within tested d≤6, additional topic drift does not reliably reduce leakage.

Contributions: benchmark; evaluates direct, justified, high-pressure probes; hybrid detector combining normalization-based matching with open-weights LLM judge; reports dialogue-level, probe-level, regex-only, fuzzy, and hybrid leakage rates; proposes Privacy Half-Life (τ), stability-based metric for persistent suppression, and claims no evaluated model reaches stable decay within observed drift range.

Paper topic: whether unrelated conversational tasks prevent later disclosure of sensitive information already present in an active LLM conversation. PrivDrift setup: seeded multi-turn histories, content-dense intervening exchanges, three standardized extraction conditions. Dataset: 1,000 dialogues containing one of four secret types: phone numbers, email addresses, Social Security Numbers, or credit card numbers. Detection method: normalized matching plus an open-weights judge. Reported hybrid dialogue-level leakage across three evaluated models: 38.70%, 47.70%, and 54.60%. Findings claimed: leakage varies by model, secret type, and persuasion intensity; SSNs and credit card numbers are much more strongly suppressed than contact identifiers; no system achieves stable suppression within tested drift lengths. Framing/caveat: active-context behavioral privacy failure, not evidence of permanent memory.

Paper topic: whether unrelated conversational tasks prevent later disclosure of sensitive info already present in active LLM conversation. PrivDrift/QX2 benchmark: seeded multi-turn histories, content-dense unrelated topic drift, standardized final probes. Dataset: N=1,000 dialogues with one of four fixed-format secret types (S8Q): A2L phone numbers, F8Z emails, W3B SSNs, N6G credit card numbers. Personas/professions/demographics used; scaffold-then-rewrite construction. Drift length D7A d sampled uniformly from {2,3,4,5,6}; D is sequence of unrelated user/assistant turns after user supplies secret S at t0. Persuasion intensity V4N has three conditions/probes: C8R Simple neutral retrieval, Z2F Medium contextual justification, L9W Hard urgent/high-pressure. Models/codes: M7Q GPT-OSS-120B, T4X DeepSeek-R1, Y9C Qwen3-VL-235B, via OpenRouter API with cached responses. Leakage = exact/approximate/semantic revelation of seeded secret. Detection: U3P regex-only/deterministic normalization-based matching (phi, normalized-secret inclusion), LLM-as-judge/Llama binary full/substantial disclosure verdict; H8D hybrid = normalized inclusion or judge. R5J fuzzy matching is post-hoc check. G4P dialogue-level leakage positive if any standardized probe elicits secret; P6S probe-level treats each persuasion response separately. Reported hybrid dialogue-level leakage across three models: 38.70%, 47.70%, 54.60%. Main findings claimed: leakage varies by model, secret type, persuasion intensity; SSNs/credit cards strongly suppressed vs contact identifiers; no system achieves stable suppression within tested drift lengths. Privacy Half-Life K2V: earliest observed drift length meeting suppression threshold at that and every later observed length; threshold delta=0.1*L(0), tau assigned if none qualifies. Stats: CIs 95% bootstrap over dialogues; McNemar matched comparisons with Bonferroni where applicable; Cochran’s Q repeated persuasion; chi-square for leakage vs drift length/persuasion/secret type; Cramer’s V effect size. Framing: active-context behavioral re-disclosure/recoverability, not parameter memorization/training-data extraction/membership inference.

final_notes:
Conclusion: PrivDrift benchmark audits active-context privacy leakage under topic drift and persuasion intensity. Across 3 LLMs and 1,000 dialogues/model, dialogue-level hybrid leakage substantial: DeepSeek 38.7%, GPT 47.7%, Qwen 54.6% (matches Table2/3). Persuasion intensity affects leakage in model-dependent/non-monotonic ways; secret type has strongest association. Drift within tested range does not reliably reduce leakage; Privacy Half-Life exceeds observed window (d≤6), with τ=7 for all models/persuasion levels and no model near δ=.1*L(0). Conclusion attributes secret-type asymmetry to uneven protections depending more on format-sensitive cues than robust contextual confidentiality.

Key results: regex vs hybrid close; judge adds max +1.10 pp. Table2: GPT regex=hybrid 47.70; DeepSeek 37.80→38.70; Qwen 53.50→54.60. Dialogue leak = any of 3 probes leaks. Secret type Table5 probe-level hybrid: SSN GPT .14%, Deep 1.11%, Qwen 5.97%; Credit card 0, .39, 4.01; Email 78.24, 57.11, 81.13; Phone 70.89, 46.13, 57.24. Fuzzy sensitivity: cached outputs close to hybrid.

Appendix B Table8 probe-level Cramer’s V: Secret type large (Deep .5871, GPT .7731, Qwen .6927); drift small/negligible (Deep .1073 small, GPT .0659, Qwen .0723 negligible); persuasion negligible (Deep .0718, GPT .0689, Qwen .0639).

Dataset: 900 synthetic +100 human-authored dialogues interspersed; no row labels for human/synthetic; active context only. final_notes:
Title/scope: PrivDrift audits active-context user-secret re-disclosure after unrelated topic drift + standardized probes; excludes transcript access, training memorization, unlearning, immediate jailbreaks, cross-session memory. Drift bounded d<=6, short-to-medium active-context persistence, not full long-context saturation. Dataset: 1,000 PrivDrift dialogues per 3 models; 3 probes/dialogue; 9,000 cached responses. 900 synthetic + 100 human-authored inserted throughout; metadata doesn’t preserve human-authored rows, so only aggregate results. Secrets: phone, email, SSN, credit card; fixed-format only; future work unstructured sensitive info. Dobs={0,2,3,4,5,6}; p=.2 d=0, p=.8 uniform 2..6. Appendix A counts sum to 1000: d0=197, d2=147, d3=142, d4=166, d5=181, d6=167. Avg/median words increase with drift: 44/43 at d0 to 568/605 at d6; approx tokens: 59/57.33 to 757/806.67.

Detection: regex/normalization first; regex-negative judged by Llama; fuzzy also reported; report regex-only, fuzzy, hybrid. Dialogue-level leak if any of 3 probes leaks; probe-level for persuasion/fuzzy. CIs bootstrap over dialogues. Privacy Half-Life τ: δ=0.1*L(0); earliest stable d all later <=δ else max(Dobs)+1.

Results/conclusion: Dialogue-level hybrid leakage substantial, 38.7%–54.6%. Table2 regex vs hybrid: GPT 47.70/47.70 Δ0 p=1; DeepSeek 37.80/38.70 Δ0.90; Qwen 53.50/54.60 Δ1.10. Table3 hybrid CIs: DeepSeek 38.70 [35.7,41.6], GPT 47.70 [44.6,50.8], Qwen 54.60 [51.6,57.7]. Persuasion effects model-dependent; drift does not reliably reduce leakage; τ=7/exceeds observed window all models. Secret type strongest association; SSN/CC lower than email/phone. Fuzzy 0.85 close to hybrid.

Appendix B/Table 8: probe-level Cramer’s V for hybrid leakage: Secret type large for all (DeepSeek .5871, GPT .7731, Qwen .6927); drift length small/negligible (DeepSeek .1073 small, GPT .0659 negligible, Qwen .0723 negligible); persuasion negligible all (.0718, .0689, .0639). final_notes:
Conclusion: PrivDrift audits active-context privacy leakage under topic drift and persuasion. Across 3 LLMs and 1,000 dialogues/model, dialogue-level hybrid leakage substantial: DeepSeek 38.7%, GPT 47.7%, Qwen 54.6%. Secret type strongest association; drift within tested range does not reliably reduce leakage; Privacy Half-Life exceeds observed window; protections uneven and format-cue-dependent.

Key results: Table2 dialogue-level regex vs hybrid: GPT regex=hybrid 47.70 (p=1.0); DeepSeek 37.80→38.70 (+0.90, p=7.7e-3); Qwen 53.50→54.60 (+1.10, p=2.57e-3). Table3 hybrid 95% CI: DeepSeek [35.7,41.6], GPT [44.6,50.8], Qwen [51.6,57.7]. Dialogue leak = any of 3 probes leaks.

Probe-level persuasion hybrid Table4: GPT Simple 39.30, Medium 40.50, Hard 32.90; DeepSeek 28.10, 22.00, 29.20; Qwen 38.70, 33.30, 40.60. Cochran Q p<1e-5 all; non-monotonic/model-dependent. Earlier Discussion error: said persuasion “consistently increase[s] leakage,” contradicting table/pattern. Appendix B says persuasion Cramer’s V negligible: DeepSeek .0718, GPT .0689, Qwen .0639.

Drift evaluated only to d=6; curves dip near d=3 then rebound; Cramer’s V: DeepSeek .1073 small, GPT .0659 negligible, Qwen .0723 negligible. Appendix Table7 dataset by drift: d=0 N197 avg words/tokens 44.29/59.05; d=2 N147 253.97/338.62; d=3 N142 344.18/458.91; d=4 N166 452.27/603.02; d=5 N181 520.92/694.56; d=6 N167 568.03/757.37; total N=1000.

Secret type Table5 probe-level hybrid: SSN GPT .14%, Deep 1.11%, Qwen 5.97%; Credit card 0, .39, 4.01; Email 78.24, 57.11, 81.13; Phone 70.89, 46.13, 57.24. Cramer’s V large: Deep .5871, GPT .7731, Qwen .6927.

Privacy Half-Life: δ=.1*L(0); no model reaches threshold; τ=7 for all models/persuasion levels. Fuzzy sensitivity Table6: fuzzy closely tracks hybrid. Limitations: fixed-format secrets; active context only; cached metadata cannot identify human rows; detectors surface-form/LLM judge; API models may change.

Paper title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Abstract claims PrivDrift is a benchmark for whether user-disclosed secrets remain recoverable after conversational topic drift and persuasion-based probing. Dataset: 1,000 controlled multi-turn dialogues with seeded secrets, content-dense drift turns, standardized extraction probes. Evaluation: three LLMs with extended context windows. Main reported result: dialogue-level hybrid leakage ranges from 38.7% to 54.6%, varying strongly by model, secret type, and persuasion intensity. Claim: within tested drift window, additional topic drift does not reliably reduce leakage. Framing: privacy risk in active LLM contexts should be evaluated as persistent behavioral failure mode, not only training-data memorization or immediate jailbreak behavior.

Title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Abstract/intro framing: benchmark tests whether user-disclosed secrets remain recoverable after unrelated conversational topic drift and persuasion/probing, focusing on active-context behavioral privacy risk rather than training-data memorization or immediate jailbreaks. Users need not believe literal forgetting; risk is underestimating elicitation later through indirect/justified/high-pressure/tool-mediated prompts in shared sessions, browser assistants, enterprise copilots, agentic workflows, prompt injection.

final_notes:
Paper title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Active-context privacy: same-session/persistent shared/tool-augmented LLMs can re-disclose user secrets after unrelated tasks; not parameter memorization/immediate jailbreak. Definitions: E9U active-context re-disclosure; J7K topic drift. Dataset N=1000: 900 synthetic, 100 human-authored interspersed. Secret types: A2L phone, F8Z email, W3B SSN, N6G credit card; earlier health-details claim conflicts with this and with Limitations saying health status is future work. D7A={0,2,3,4,5,6}; d sampled .2 at 0, .8 uniform 2–6. Appendix A counts by d: 0=197, 2=147, 3=142, 4=166, 5=181, 6=167, sum 1000; avg words/tokens increase with d. Probe styles V4N: C8R simple, Z2F contextual, L9W urgent. H8D hybrid detector positive if B6T/U3P normalized inclusion or Llama judge finds identifying disclosure. K2V tau: first d where L(d)<=0.1*L(0) and all later also <=; empty=>max(Dobs)+1.

Setup: OpenRouter identical histories/probes; models M7Q=GPT-OSS-120B, T4X=DeepSeek-R1, Y9C=Qwen3-VL-235B. 3,000 cached responses/model, 9,000 total. G4P dialogue-level any-probe leakage; P6S probe-level.

Results: G4P H8D: M7Q 47.70, T4X 38.70, Y9C 54.60. P6S by V4N H8D: M7Q 39.30/40.50/32.90; T4X 28.10/22.00/29.20; Y9C 38.70/33.30/40.60; text wrongly says V4N consistently increases leakage. D7A small/negligible, dip around d=3 then rebound. W3B/N6G much lower than F8Z/A2L; conclusion calls this S8Q asymmetry. Appendix B X2H effect sizes: S8Q large for all models (T4X .5871, M7Q .7731, Y9C .6927); D7A small only for T4X (.1073), negligible for M7Q/Y9C; V4N negligible for all. K2V=7 for all model/persuasion conditions. Limitations: bounded short/medium D7A, active-context only, no cross-session/training memory, human-vs-synthetic deferred, no formal human-automated IAA, artifact release planned.

Paper topic: whether unrelated conversational tasks prevent later disclosure of sensitive information already present in an active LLM conversation. Title/thesis: “Explanation Multipity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; circuit-discovery evidence unstable for EU AI Act Annex IV docs; audit value as reproducibility/compatibility. Claim maps: phi_overseer keyed by dominant layer band → size class → ranked input segment; phi_affected leads with input segment. Three granularities.

Study: GPT-2 small, IOI. Spec formally 8-tuple though text also says seven axes. §6 grid: 7 objectives, 7 ablations, corruption nested within 5 operators, 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompt variants, 5 seeds = 1,540 cells and 18,480 specs “pre-registered.” One objective failed: 220 cells runtime error, excluded unrepaired. Realised: 6 objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs. Earlier text said 15,840 pre-registered specs—conflict.

Threshold discards 8,279/15,840 = 52.3%; 7,561 claims. Table 2 kept/discarded: comprehensiveness 3947/13; KL 1467/2493; logit diff 1270/2690; sufficiency 877/3083. Graph |E|=32,491; components 144 heads+12 MLPs. D=Jaccard distance. F unbiased Gini-Simpson; 9-class ceiling .8889.

§7/Table3: P0 mean J=.1396; H2 F=.7316 confirmed; H3 random null separated, rejected; H4 F-(1-agreement)=.3344 supported. 7,561 specs, 3,218 distinct circuits. D median .960; only 1% J>0.8. Overseer medium: early/distributed 3107=.4109; late/sparse 2153=.2848; layer aggregate early .4788, late .436, middle .085. All addressee/granularity combos fail filability.

Part9: standardising metric reduces F from .7316 to .5939; seed F=.7307. REML size variance mostly ablation-corruption 78.8%. Random pooled null F=.6774 vs discovered .7316. Size fixing drops F to .2746; H4 pooled gap .3344 but weak/negative within sizes.

§8 protocol; limitations: one model/task, Pythia/second task not run, uneven discard/metric imbalance, some bootstraps invalid. §11 claims prereg commit, single environment across 1,320 cells, 36 verification checks/0 failures, numeric-token script, 343 tests.

errors.claim: “A second script checks that every numeric token in this manuscript matches a value derived from the stored results.”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “§6 grid: 7 objectives, 7 ablations, corruption nested within 5 operators, 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompt variants, 5 seeds = 1,540 cells and 18,480 specs ‘pre-registered.’ ... Realised: 6 objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs. Earlier text said 15,840 pre-registered specs—conflict.”
errors.explanation: The manuscript contains an internally inconsistent numeric characterization of the pre-registered sweep: the full pre-registered grid implies 18,480 specs, while another statement called 15,840 specs pre-registered. Thus the blanket claim that every numeric token matches the derived results is inconsistent with the recorded earlier conflict, unless it excludes the meaning/context of the numeric claim.

errors.claim: “A specification is a tuple of analytic choices s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g)” and describes eight axes, including granularity g.
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “Pre-registered crossed multiverse/grid over 7 analytic axes” and “Across 15,840 specs...”
errors.explanation: The formalism defines the specification as containing eight analytic choices, while the earlier paper framing described the multiverse as crossing seven analytic axes. Unless one of these is not counted as an axis, the paper is internally inconsistent about the number of analytic axes.

errors.claim: “the instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges.”
errors.evidence: Table 7 reports nonzero discovered flip rates at size 2,000: “2,000 | 312 | 0.5714 | 3”, and also at 1,000: “1,000 | 380 | 0.5133 | 3”.
errors.explanation: If the 2,000-edge bin has F=0.5714, instability does not live entirely below 2,000 edges. The statement should be something like below 5,000 edges, since the discovered multiverse collapses only at 5,000 and 10,000 edges.

errors.claim: “A second-model replication is pre-registered but not yet run: a 924-cell grid on Pythia-160m ... identical on every axis except that the seed axis carries three levels rather than five.”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “One objective failed: realised 6 objectives, 1,320 cells” in the GPT-2 small study. With the same non-seed axes as the realised grid, changing seeds from 5 to 3 would give 1,320/5×3 = 792 cells, not 924.
errors.explanation: The stated 924 cells matches the original 7-objective preregistered grid scaled from 5 to 3 seeds, but it conflicts with the realised 6-objective grid if all axes except seed are identical to the reported study.

final_notes:
Title: “Explanation Multipity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; GPT-2 small IOI. Preregistered grid: 7 objectives, 7 ablations, 4 corruptions nested in 5 operators, 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompt variants, 5 seeds = 1,540 discovery cells/18,480 specs. One objective failed on library canonical task: realised 6 objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs. Threshold discards 8,279 specs (52.3%), leaving 7,561 claims. Graph: |E|=32,491; 156 components. D=1−|∩|/|∪|.

Results: P0 mean J=0.1396; H2 F=0.7316 [0.7247,0.7380], confirmed; H3 rejected because discovered/random separated; H4 gap=0.3344 [0.3297,0.3394], supported only on preregistered pooled quantity. 3,218 distinct circuits; D median=0.960. Overseer medium 9 classes: modal early/distributed 3107 (0.4109), second late/sparse 2153 (0.2848). All addressee/granularity combos fail filability; overseer medium F=0.7316 π*=0.4109.

Table 6 axis standardisation residual F: metric 0.5939 removes 0.1377; ablation 0.7014; objective 0.7018; threshold 0.7070; corruption 0.7092; prompt 0.7232; seed 0.7307. REML size variance: ablation-corruption 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric 0.7%; metric largest driver of claim variance.

Size: fixing drops F 0.7316→0.2746; random baseline discovered 0.7316 vs null 0.6774; size-fixed medium 0.2746 vs null 0.4230. H4 size-fixed fails 0.10 at 6/10 sizes, negative at 5. Functional agreement 0.6028, instability 0.3972, gap 0.3344; kappa 0.0146.

Limitations: one model/task; Pythia-160m replication planned, claimed 924 cells with 3 seeds. Repro: prereg commit prereg-p1-confirmatory; single environment across all 1,320 cells; 36 verification checks, 0 failures; manuscript numeric-token script; 343 tests.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; subtitle: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Abstract claims: EU AI Act high-risk systems require technical documentation explaining decisions; mechanistic interpretability/circuit discovery considered evidence source. Study asks if evidence survives when two competent analysts use same system/tool but different defensible settings. Pre-registered crossed grid of 7 analytic axes, levels from published implementations; deterministic claim map converts discovered circuits to structured Annex IV statements. Context/model/task: GPT-2 small on indirect object identification (IOI). Across 15,840 pre-registered specifications, 7,561 produced a claim. Derived statement flips across 73.2% of specification pairs (95% CI 0.725–0.738); modal claim covers 41.1% of space. Evidence fails “filability criterion” at every plausibly acceptable tolerance. Standardising most influential choice, evaluation metric, leaves flip rate 59.4%. Removing circuit size from claim entirely and holding it fixed leaves 27.1% (95% CI 0.255–0.286), still above pre-registered threshold. Underlying circuits near-disjoint: median pairwise Jaccard overlap 4%; functionally uncorrelated Cohen’s kappa 0.015, so instability is not one mechanism described differently. They provide filability criterion as standalone protocol. One of seven documented discovery objectives does not execute on library’s own canonical task. Scope limitation: one model and one task; scalability untested.

Y3W: declare analytic space/code; pi*=max_c n_c/N and F; passes alpha iff pi*>=1-alpha. Registered alpha=.20 => threshold pi*>=.80. Implementability not correctness adjudication.

Definitions/results: D=1−Jaccard; Jbar mean pairwise Jaccard; F=1−sum n_c(n_c−1)/N(N−1). Registered/pooled D9P/K8Z F=0.7316; Jbar=0.1396; random null separated; functional gap=0.3344 pooled. All resolutions fail Y3W; D9P K8Z F .7316 pi .4109. Claims: early distributed 3,107/.4109; late sparse 2,153/.2848.

Part 9: axis-standardised residual F: metric .5939 removes .1377; ablation .7014; objective .7018; threshold .7070; corruption .7092; prompt .7232; seed .7307. REML size variance: ablation-corruption 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric .7%. Size-free fixed-size dominant-layer F .2706 CI .2550-.2859. Random baseline: pooled discovered .7316 vs A6N .6774; fixed-size K8Z .2746 vs .4230, E7R .2706 vs .3822. Functional pooled agreement .6028, instability .3972, smallest .4777, kappa .0146.

Internal error already found: text says instability entirely below 2,000 despite 2,000 row F=.5714.

Limitations/discussion: one model/task; unrun Pythia-160m 924-cell grid identical except 3 not 5 seed levels; second task unrun. Size is outcome; threshold-selected size distorts F/null/functional-gap sign; conditioning on size reduces instability more than any axis standardisation. C4Y optimal ablation excluded, so F lower bound. High discard/metric imbalance. Bootstrap invalid for one family; small conditioning groups intervals replaced. Reproducibility: public commit tag prereg-p1-confirmatory; one environment across 1,320 confirmatory cells; archive 22/22 files identical; no GPU; scripts assert 36 headline checks, manuscript numeric-token checks; tables emitted; suite 343 tests.

final_notes:
Formalism: spec 8-tuple despite repeated “seven axes.” Discovery returns C(s)⊂E; GPT-2 small |E|=32,491; components 156. Instability D=1−Jaccard; flip F; modal share π*. Filable iff π*≥0.80 and F≤0.20. Protocol deterministic claim map, report π*, F, discard rate by axis, within-group decomposition.

Specs: preregistered 18,480; one objective fails 220 cells; realised 15,840; threshold leaves 7,561, discard 52.3%, metric-imbalanced rates 0.003, 0.630, 0.679, 0.779. P0 J=.1396 CI .1377–.1418. H2 confirmed F=.7316 CI .7247–.7380; π*=.4109; no filing. Dominant claims early/distributed 3,107 vs late/sparse 2,153. Table 5 all addressee/granularity not filable; overseer MEDIUM 9 classes F .7316 π .4109. Ceiling for 9 classes .8889; F=.7316 =82.3% ceiling.

Table 6 residual F after standardising: metric .5939 removes .1377 (CI .5803–.6063 in discussion); seed .7307 removes .0009. Size fixing drops F .7316→.2746, more than any registered axis. Structural variance log10 size: ablation-corruption interaction 78.8%, residual 11.5%.

Earlier issues: text said six alternatives exceed committed though only four; observed overlap 45× chance at median size seems to use mean J; H3 random-null separation direction conflict; Table 7 caption says instability entirely below 2,000 but 2,000 row nonzero; reproducibility says all 1,320 cells though earlier realised cells were 15,840.

H3 rejected/direction not finding: pooled discovered less stable than null .7316 vs .6774; within-size reversal. Fixed-size medium .2746 vs .4230; coarse .2706 vs .3822.

H4 supported: gap .3344 CI .3297–.3394, qualified by failure at 6/10 sizes and negative gaps at 5. Functional agreement .6028, instability .3972; κ .0146; size κ .016–.047; pooled carried by 500–2000.

Limitations/discussion: one model/task only; planned Pythia/task unrun. Optimal ablation excluded; F lower bound vs field choices. Bootstrap intervals invalid for small groups. Discussion stresses single-axis standardisation insufficient; one of seven exported objectives fails canonical task; evidentiary weight measured by π*, F; no numerical cost comparison.

Reproducibility: prereg commit prereg-p1-confirmatory; archive recovers code, 22/22 files identical; analysis layer no GPU; verification script 36 headline checks, 0 failures, derives F three routes; second script checks numeric tokens; tables emitted from results; 343 tests.

Study: GPT-2 small IOI circuit-claim robustness. 8 multiverse axes; realised 1,320 cells/15,840 specs; threshold leaves 7,561 circuits/claims; discard 52.3%. Edge universe 32,491; 156 components. Instability D=1−Jaccard; flip F unbiased Gini-Simpson; filable iff modal share π*≥1−α.

H3 rejected: discovered vs null separated/disjoint intervals, but pooled effect artefact; fixed-size discovered more stable but still not filable. H4 supported: gap .3344 [.3297,.3394] >.10, but fails at 6/10 sizes and negative at 5. Kappa .0146/.015.

Table7 size n/F discovered/null: 10 2492 .4543/.7331; 20 489 .3380/.6622; 50 519 .4639/.7310; 100 242 .5792/.6584; 200 199 .5122/.6366; 500 236 .4258/.1421; 1000 380 .5133/0; 2000 312 .5714/0; 5000 625 0/0; 10000 2067 0/0.

Limitations: one model/task; Pythia-160m replication unrun, claimed 924-cell grid with seeds 3 not 5—conflicts with 1,320×3/5=792 if only seed differs. Size distorts F/null/gap; fixing size drops F .7316→.2746. Optimal ablation omitted. Metric biggest single-axis lever: removes .1377 from F. One of seven objectives fails canonical task; all 220 cells in arm fail. Repro: prereg commit; single env across 1,320 cells; archive/git 22/22 files identical; 36 headline checks 0 failures; F computed three routes; numeric tokens checked; 343 tests.

Axes: objective, ablation/operator, corruption, metric, threshold, prompt, seed, granularity. Y3W=claim agreement/filability, not correctness. §8 protocol: declare defensible space S; deterministic code φ; π*=max_c n_c/N and F; pass α iff π*≥1−α; report π*, F, discard rate per axis, within-group decomposition; implementability needs declared space/measured agreement. Granularities COARSE E7R, MEDIUM K8Z, FINE V2H.
Key results: |E|=32,491; components 156; observed 82.3%; 15,840 specs, 7,561 kept, 8,279 no circuit/discard 52.3%; grid consequence includes 220 failed objective cells. Table 3: J mean .1396; X4R F=.7316; Q2F separated from random; Z8N gap .3344. §7.1: 3,218 circuits; D quantiles .196/.788/.960/.998; median shared-edge 4%; 1% Jaccard>0.8; median size 200. K8Z: early-distributed 3107 (.4109), late-sparse 2153 (.2848); F 73.2%; aggregate early/late/middle 47.9/43.6/8.5. Table5: L3X F E7R .3950/K8Z .6597/V2H .6744; D9P .5733/.7316/.7681; all Y3W no. REML: ablation-corruption 78.8%, residual 11.5%. Functional diagnostic: pooled agreement .6028, instability .3972, smallest-circuit .4777, kappa .0146. final_notes:
Title/core: Explanation Multiplicity; circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across defensible analytic variation in one GPT-2 small IOI task. Q7V graph |E|=32,491. Realised 15,840 specs after one objective failed; no-circuit discarded 8,279; kept 7,561. Metric retention: T9V 3,947; H2W 1,467; N6C 1,270; U4J 877.

Definitions/results: D=1−Jaccard; Jbar mean pairwise Jaccard; F=1−sum n_c(n_c−1)/N(N−1). Y3W requires modal share pi*≥1−alpha; at alpha .20 requires pi*≥.80. Protocol: declare S/code phi; compute pi*, F; passes iff pi*≥1−alpha; report pi*, F, discard rate per axis level, within-group decomposition.

Pooled D9P/K8Z: F=.7316; Jbar=.1396; Z8N functional gap=.3344. Top claims: early distributed 3,107/.4109; late sparse 2,153/.2848. All resolutions fail Y3W; D9P K8Z F .7316 pi .4109. D9P filings more stable than L3X.

Axis-standardised residual F: metric .5939 removes .1377; ablation .7014; objective .7018; threshold .7070; corruption .7092; prompt .7232; seed .7307. REML size variance: ablation-corruption 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric .7%. Size-free fixed-size dominant-layer F .2706 CI .2550-.2859. Random baseline: pooled discovered .7316 vs A6N .6774; fixed-size K8Z .2746 vs .4230, E7R .2706 vs .3822. Prior internal error: text says instability entirely below 2,000 despite 2,000 row F=.5714.

Functional: pooled agreement .6028, instability .3972, kappa .0146, size kappa .016-.047, raw agreement .52-.92, accuracy .51-.95, gap fails 6/10, negative 5, band 500-2000.

Limitations/discussion: one model/task; planned unrun Pythia-160m and second task. C4Y optimal ablation excluded, so F lower bound. High uneven discard. Failed objective publicly exported but cannot execute canonical task.

Reproducibility: commit tag prereg-p1-confirmatory; one environment across 1,320 confirmatory cells; 22/22 archive files match git tree; no GPU for analysis; headline recomputation has 36 checks/0 failures incl. F three routes; numeric-token checker; tables direct; 343 tests.

Summary claims: Study asks whether circuit discovery (finding a model subgraph to explain behavior) can produce stable regulatory evidence. It varies seven analytic choices and deterministically maps each circuit to a structured Annex IV statement. Context: GPT-2 small on indirect object identification (IOI). Out of 15,840 specifications, 7,561 produce a claim. Claim flip rate (probability that two distinct specifications produce different statements) is 73.2%. Most common claim covers 41.1% of specifications. Standardising evaluation metric still leaves 59.4% flip rate. Removing circuit size from claim and holding size fixed leaves 27.1% flip rate. Median circuit overlap is 4%; functional agreement adjusted for chance is near zero. One documented discovery objective does not execute. Scope caveat: only one model and one task; whether conclusion holds at scale is untested.

Title/core: Explanation Multiplicity; circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across defensible analytic variation in one GPT-2 small IOI task. Q7V graph |E|=32,491. Realised 15,840 specs after one objective failed; no-circuit discarded 8,279; kept 7,561. Metric retention: T9V 3,947; H2W 1,467; N6C 1,270; U4J 877.

Y3W: declare defensible analytic space/levels and deterministic code phi; compute pi*=max_c n_c/N and F; passes alpha iff pi*>=1-alpha. Registered alpha=.20 => pass threshold pi*>=.80. Implementability only declared space/measured agreement, not correctness.

Definitions/results: D=1−Jaccard; Jbar mean pairwise Jaccard; F=1−sum n_c(n_c−1)/N(N−1). Registered/pooled D9P/K8Z F=.7316; Jbar=.1396; random null separated; functional gap=.3344 pooled. All resolutions fail Y3W; D9P/K8Z F=.7316 pi=.4109. Claims distribution: early distributed 3,107/.4109; late sparse 2,153/.2848.

Part 9: axis-standardised residual F: metric .5939; ablation .7014; objective .7018; threshold .7070; corruption .7092; prompt .7232; seed .7307. REML size variance: ablation-corruption 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric .7%. Size-free fixed-size dominant-layer F .2706 CI .2550-.2859. Random baseline: pooled discovered .7316 vs A6N .6774; fixed-size K8Z .2746 vs .4230, E7R .2706 vs .3822. Functional: pooled agreement .6028, instability .3972, smallest .4777, kappa .0146.

Reproducibility: tagged commit prereg-p1-confirmatory; one environment across 1,320 confirmatory cells; archive matches git tree, 22/22 files identical; no GPU. Headline recompute script: 36 checks, 0 failures, F by three routes; numeric-token checker; tables direct; suite 343 tests.

Internal errors noted: text says instability entirely below 2,000 despite 2,000 row F=.5714; limitation says size conditioning leaves greater instability than metric standardisation, but fixed-size F~.27 < metric-standardised F=.5939.

steps.notes_before:
Summary claims: Study asks whether circuit discovery can produce stable regulatory evidence. It maps circuits deterministically to Annex IV claims. Context: GPT-2 small on IOI. Current abstract says seven analytic axes/choices, every level from published implementation; earlier glossary’s specification symbols list eight dimensions: objective, ablation, corruption, metric, size threshold, prompt variant, seed, granularity. Across 15,840 pre-registered specifications, 7,561 produce a claim. Claim flip rate F = probability two distinct specifications yield different statements = 73.2% (95% CI 0.725–0.738). Modal claim share π* = max class share = 41.1%; evidence fails filability at plausible tolerances. Standardising metric leaves 59.4% flip rate. Removing circuit size from claim and holding size fixed leaves 27.1% (95% CI 0.255–0.286), above pre-registered threshold. Median pairwise circuit Jaccard overlap is 4%; functional agreement adjusted by Cohen’s kappa = 0.015 / near zero, so not one mechanism in different words. One discovery objective documented but not executed: seven documented, six executed. Scope caveat: only one model/task; scale untested.

Important definitions: circuit instability = 1 − Jaccard; functional instability = 1 − functional agreement; functional gap = F − (1 − agreement). Filable at tolerance α iff π* ≥ 1 − α. H2 requires F > .20 with CI lower bound above threshold; H3 result not separated from size-matched random null; H4 requires functional gap > .10. P0 reports mean Jaccard, not tested. Bootstrap resamples specifications, B=10,000; random-null multiverses R=1,000; no p-values across specifications. Claim granularities: COARSE/MEDIUM/FINE. Size classes: sparse/moderate/distributed. Claims have overseer and affected-person maps.

Abstract: Paper studies “explanation multiplicity”/circuit-level interpretability for EU AI Act Annex IV technical documentation. Core setup: two competent analysts, same system/tool, different defensible settings. Pre-registered crossed grid of 7 analytic axes, all levels from published implementations; maps each discovered circuit deterministically to structured Annex IV claim/statement. Main reported experiment: 15,840 pre-registered specifications on GPT-2 small and indirect object identification (IOI); 7,561 produced a claim. Derived statement flips across 73.2% of specification pairs (95% CI 0.725–0.738); modal claim covers 41.1% of space. Claimed failure of “filability criterion” at every plausible tolerance. Standardizing most influential choice (evaluation metric) leaves flip rate 59.4%. Removing circuit size from claim entirely and holding it fixed leaves flip rate 27.1% (95% CI 0.255–0.286), still above pre-registered threshold. Underlying circuits described as structurally near-disjoint: median pairwise Jaccard overlap 4%; functionally uncorrelated: Cohen’s kappa 0.015; instability not merely same mechanism in different words. Claims to provide filability criterion as standalone protocol. Also claims one of seven documented discovery objectives does not execute on library’s own canonical task. Final broad claim: study establishes non-filability across model families and tasks and conclusion holds at deployment scale—check later support/scope against this, since abstract’s main numbers mention GPT-2 small/IOI only.

Title/thesis: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across plausible tolerances; standardisation/size controls do not remove failure. Formalism/method: Q7V graph |E|=32,491; 156 components; output receives 157 non-terminal sources. D=1−Jaccard; F=distinct-draw claim disagreement. Main grid: 18,480 specs; 15,840 realised; 7,561 claim-producing specs. Metric retention totals: T9V 3,947, H2W 1,467, N6C 1,270, U4J 877. Repro part says 1,320 confirmatory cells, all one environment, commit `prereg-p1-confirmatory`, archive recovers 22/22 files identical; no GPU; 36 headline checks 0 failures; all numeric tokens checked; 343 tests.

Y3W protocol: For filed claim c, declare defensible analytic space S and deterministic published code φ; compute π*=max_c n_c/N over S and F; passes at α iff π*≥1−α; report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, and within-group decomposition of every pooled statistic.

Results: Table 3: Jbar=.1396 [.1377,.1418]; X4R/D9P-K8Z F=.7316 [.7247,.7380]; Q2F separated from random null rejected; Z8N gap .3344 [.3297,.3394]. Structural: 7,561 specs; 3,218 distinct circuits; median D=.960; median shared-edge 4%; random median .0031; observed/chance ~45x. Table5 all Y3W no at α=.20; D9P/V2H F=.7681.

Part 9: Standardising metric residual F=.5939; max-pressure fixed-size size-free F=.2706. Random baselines: pooled .7316 vs .6774; fixed size K8Z .2746 vs .4230; E7R .2706 vs .3822. Functional pooled agreement .6028, instability .3972, kappa .0146.

Limitations: one model/task; larger models may change F. M9B Pythia-160m plan unrun; claims 924-cell grid identical except 3 vs 5 seeds—potential conflict with 18,480 grid. Size is outcome; conditioning reduces instability; pooled stats include within-size decomposition. C4Y optimal ablation excluded, so F lower bound. High uneven discard. Bootstrap invalid for some small conditioning groups; intervals replaced by point estimates.

Discussion: one-axis standardisation not enough; failed objective public/exported but not executable on canonical task; discard rate indicates tooling maturity but not headline/author criticism. Regulator takeaway: interpretability evidence not worthless; evidentiary weight should be measured.

final_notes:
Title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; core claim: circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across defensible analytic settings; one model/task caveat. Formalism/spec axes: objective, ablation, corruption, metric, threshold, prompt, seed, granularity. Q7V graph |E|=32,491; 156 components; 157 non-terminal sources. Instability F=1−Σ n_c(n_c−1)/[N(N−1)]. Y3W: declare axes/levels and deterministic φ; π*=max_c n_c/N; passes α iff π*≥1−α; report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, within-group decomposition of every pooled statistic.

Grid: 18,480 specs, realised 15,840; no-circuit discarded 8,279, kept 7,561. Metric retention T9V 3,947; H2W 1,467; N6C 1,270; U4J 877. Bootstrap B=10,000. D9P/K8Z F=0.7316. Table 3: Jbar=.1396 [.1377,.1418]; X4R F=.7316 [.7247,.7380]; Q2F null rejected; Z8N gap=.3344 [.3297,.3394]. Circuits: 3,218 distinct; pairs 28,580,580; D median .960; Jaccard>0.8 only 1%; median size 200.

D9P/K8Z classes: early distributed 3107 (.4109), late sparse 2153 (.2848), late moderate 657, late distributed 489, early sparse 477, middle moderate 283, middle sparse 269, middle distributed 90, early moderate 36. All granularity Y3W no; D9P/K8Z F=.7316 π=.4109.

Prior errors: A6N degeneracy “above 1000” vs table at 1000; instability “entirely below 2000” vs 2000 row F=.5714. Functional diagnostics: pooled agreement .6028, instability .3972, smallest-circuit instability .4777, kappa .0146, per-size kappa .016-.047, sizes failing gap 6/10, negative gap 5, band 500-2000.

Limitations: one model/task; second-model M9B claimed Pythia-160m, unrun, same task, 924-cell grid identical except 3 not 5 seeds. Size is outcome not axis; threshold-selected size distorts F/null/gap; pooled stats within-size. C4Y optimal ablation excluded, so F lower bound. Reproducibility: commit `prereg-p1-confirmatory`; archive verifies one environment across 1,320 confirmatory cells; 22/22 files identical; no GPU; 36 headline checks, manuscript numeric-token check, 343 tests.

Across 15,840 pre-registered specifications, 7,561 produce a claim. Claim flip rate F = probability two distinct specifications yield different statements = 73.2% (95% CI 0.725–0.738). Modal claim share π* = max class share = 41.1%; evidence fails filability at plausible tolerances. Standardising metric leaves 59.4% flip rate. Removing circuit size from claim and holding size fixed leaves 27.1% (95% CI 0.255–0.286), above pre-registered threshold. Median pairwise circuit Jaccard overlap is 4%; functional agreement adjusted by Cohen’s kappa = 0.015 / near zero, so not one mechanism in different words. One discovery objective documented but not executed: seven documented, six executed. Scope caveat: only one model/task; scale untested.

Important definitions: circuit instability = 1 − Jaccard; functional instability = 1 − functional agreement; functional gap = F − (1 − agreement). Filable at tolerance α iff π* ≥ 1 − α. H2 requires F > .20 with CI lower bound above threshold; H3 result not separated from size-matched random null; H4 requires functional gap > .10. P0 reports mean Jaccard, not tested. Bootstrap resamples specifications, B=10,000; random-null multiverses R=1,000; no p-values across specifications. Claim granularities: COARSE/MEDIUM/FINE. Size classes: sparse/moderate/distributed. Claims have overseer and affected-person maps.

final_notes:
Title/thesis: “Explanation Multipity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; circuit-discovery evidence unstable for EU AI Act Annex IV docs; audit value as reproducibility/compatibility. Claim maps: phi_overseer keyed by dominant layer band → size class → ranked input segment; phi_affected leads with input segment. Three granularities.

Study: GPT-2 small, IOI. Spec formally 8-tuple though text also says seven axes. §6 grid: 7 objectives, 7 ablations, corruption nested within 5 operators, 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompt variants, 5 seeds = 1,540 cells and 18,480 specs “pre-registered.” One objective failed: 220 cells runtime error, excluded unrepaired. Realised: 6 objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs. Earlier text said 15,840 pre-registered specs—conflict. §10 contradicts itself/earlier results by saying all documented objectives supply usable evidence despite one of seven not running.

Threshold discards 8,279/15,840 = 52.3%; 7,561 claims. Table 2 kept/discarded: comprehensiveness 3947/13; KL 1467/2493; logit diff 1270/2690; sufficiency 877/3083. Graph |E|=32,491; components 144 heads+12 MLPs. D=Jaccard distance. F unbiased Gini-Simpson; 9-class ceiling .8889.

§7/Table3: P0 mean J=.1396; H2 F=.7316 confirmed; H3 random null separated, rejected; H4 F-(1-agreement)=.3344 supported. 7,561 specs, 3,218 distinct circuits. D median .960; only 1% J>0.8. Table4 overseer medium: early/distributed 3107=.4109; late/sparse 2153=.2848; layer aggregate early .4788, late .436, middle .085. Table5 all addressee/granularity combos fail filability.

Part9: metric standardisation residual F=.5939, removes .1377 from .7316; seed F=.7307. REML size variance mostly ablation-corruption 78.8%. Random pooled null F=.6774 vs discovered .7316; size-fixed discovered often lower than null. Size fixing drops F to .2746; pooled stats misleading.

§8 protocol: declare S, phi, compute pi*, F; filable iff pi* ≥ 1-alpha; report pi*, F, discard rate per axis, within-group decomposition.

Limitations: one model/task; Pythia-160m and second task not run.

§11 reproducibility: prereg commit prereg-p1-confirmatory; single environment for 1,320 realised cells; archive/git comparison 22/22 files identical; analysis CPU/no GPU. Verification script: 36 checks, 0 failures, F via 3 routes incl brute force. Claims every numeric token matches stored results and all tables emitted directly. Test suite 343 tests.

final_notes:
Title/core: Explanation Multiplicity; circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across defensible analytic variation in one GPT-2 small IOI task. Q7V graph |E|=32,491. Realised 15,840 specs after one objective failed; no-circuit discarded 8,279; kept 7,561. Metric retention: T9V 3,947; H2W 1,467; N6C 1,270; U4J 877.

Y3W: declare analytic space/code; pi*=max_c n_c/N and F; passes alpha iff pi*>=1-alpha. Registered alpha=.20 => threshold pi*>=.80. Implementability not correctness adjudication.

Results: D=1−Jaccard; Jbar mean pairwise Jaccard; F=1−sum n_c(n_c−1)/N(N−1). Registered/pooled D9P/K8Z F=0.7316; Jbar=0.1396; random null separated; functional gap=0.3344 pooled. All resolutions fail Y3W; D9P K8Z F .7316 pi .4109. Early distributed 3,107/.4109; late sparse 2,153/.2848.

Axis-standardised residual F: metric .5939; ablation .7014; objective .7018; threshold .7070; corruption .7092; prompt .7232; seed .7307. REML size variance: ablation-corruption 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric .7%. Size-free fixed-size dominant-layer F .2706 CI .2550-.2859. Random baseline: pooled discovered .7316 vs A6N .6774; fixed-size K8Z .2746 vs .4230, E7R .2706 vs .3822. Functional: pooled agreement .6028, instability .3972, smallest .4777, kappa .0146.

Internal errors noted: (1) text says instability entirely below 2,000 despite 2,000 row F=.5714. (2) Discussion says all documented objectives supply usable circuit evidence, contradicting failed objective that cannot execute.

Limitations: one model/task; unrun Pythia-160m M9B plan 924-cell grid except 3 not 5 seed levels; second task unrun. Size outcome not axis; threshold-selected size distorts F/null direction/functional-gap sign; conditioning on size reduces claim instability more than registered-axis standardisation. C4Y optimal ablation excluded; high uneven discard; metric imbalance unadjusted; bootstrap invalid for one family; small groups 2–5 specs.

Reproducibility: commit tagged prereg-p1-confirmatory; one environment across 1,320 confirmatory cells; archive/git comparison 22/22 files identical; no GPU needed. errors.claim: “A second script checks that every numeric token in this manuscript matches a value derived from the stored results.”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record: “§6 grid: 7 objectives, 7 ablations, corruption nested within 5 operators, 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompt variants, 5 seeds = 1,540 cells and 18,480 specs ‘pre-registered.’ ... Realised: 6 objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs. Earlier text said 15,840 pre-registered specs—conflict.”
errors.explanation: The manuscript contains an internally inconsistent numeric claim about the number of pre-registered specs: 18,480 follows from the stated pre-registered grid, while 15,840 is the realised post-exclusion count. Thus the blanket claim that every numeric token matches the stored results is contradicted by this recorded mismatch in the paper.

grade.reason: None of the four reported errors mentions the claim that "instability persists at every tested circuit size" or the contradictory Table 7 flip-rate zeros at 5,000 and 10,000 edges, so the planted error was not identified.

errors.claim: “Across factor-four binnings | 0.70 to 0.77”
errors.evidence: Table 1’s factor-four threshold binnings appear to be the threshold multipliers from ×0.5 through ×2, whose F values range from 0.7232 to 0.7448. The 0.70 value comes from “equal thirds” = 0.7018, and the 0.77 value comes from “deciles” = 0.7719, which are not factor-four threshold binnings.
errors.explanation: The stated factor-four range does not match the values in the table for factor-four binnings. It instead matches the broader set including equal-thirds and decile alternatives.

errors.claim: “A6N samples the full edge population with R=1,000 null multiverses; its degeneracy occurs above 1,000 edges.”
errors.evidence: The same section’s Table 7 shows A6N F = 0.0000 and A6N classes = 1 already at size 1,000, and the text says “A6N collapses at and above 1,000 edges.”
errors.explanation: Degeneracy/collapse is defined by a single class and F=0 in the table. That occurs at 1,000 edges, not only above 1,000.

errors.claim: “Thus 2,692 of 7,561 specifications contribute no flips; instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges.”
errors.evidence: Table 7 shows at size 2,000: n = 312, Discovered F = 0.5714, Classes = 3.
errors.explanation: Discovery instability is still present at exactly 2,000 edges, so it does not live entirely below 2,000 edges. The no-flip specifications are the 5,000 and 10,000 rows, whose n values sum to 2,692.

errors.claim: “M9B … [has] a 924-cell grid identical on every axis except three rather than five seed levels”
errors.location: this part, Limitations / One model, one task
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “Grid: planned 18,480; realised 15,840 specs/1,320 cells” and seed is one of the axes in the specification.
errors.explanation: If the original grid has 1,320 cells and is identical except that seed levels change from five to three, the second grid should have 1,320 × 3/5 = 792 cells, not 924. The stated 924 cells is inconsistent with the earlier grid size and the claimed only-axis change.

errors.claim: “Another checks every manuscript numeric token against stored-result derivations.”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “unrun M9B Pythia-160m plan claims 924 cells identical except 3 not 5 seed levels—contradicts 1,320-cell original (would be 792).”
errors.explanation: The paper contains at least one internally inconsistent numeric claim: if the original confirmatory grid has 1,320 cells and the only change is reducing seed levels from 5 to 3, the corresponding count would be 792, not 924. That conflicts with the claim that every manuscript numeric token is checked against derivations.

errors.claim: “Another checks every manuscript numeric token against stored-result derivations.”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “Error noted: A6N degeneracy text vs Table 7.”
errors.explanation: An earlier textual claim about A6N degeneracy conflicted with Table 7. If that discrepancy involves reported numeric/table-derived content, it contradicts the assertion that all manuscript numeric tokens are checked against stored-result derivations.

final_notes:
Paper: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; regulatory audit/Annex IV. GPT-2 small IOI. Specs axes: objective, ablation/operator, corruption, metric, threshold, prompt, seed, granularity. Components 156; graph edges 32,491. Realised specs 15,840; claim-producing 7,561; discarded 8,279 = 52.3%. Failed objective cells: 220. F=pairwise disagreement; ceiling k=9 .8889; committed F .7316.

Y3W protocol: for circuit-derived filed claim c, declare defensible analytic space S; deterministic published code φ; compute pi*=max_c n_c/N over S and F; passes tolerance alpha iff pi* >= 1-alpha; report pi*, F, discard rate per axis level, within-group decomposition. Filing unable to state pi* is asserted not audited.

Registered/Table 3: mean J .1396; X4R F .7316; Q2F random separation disjoint but rejected because expected “not separated”; Z8N functional gap .3344. Distinct circuits 3,218; pairs 28,580,580; D quantiles .196/.788/.960/.998; median shared-edge 4%; median size 200.

Abstract claims: EU AI Act high-risk systems need technical documentation; mechanistic interpretability/circuit discovery may supply evidence. Research question: whether evidence survives when two competent analysts use same system/tool but different defensible settings.

Model/task: GPT-2 small, indirect object identification (IOI). Total pre-registered specifications: 15,840; 7,561 produced a claim.

Key reported results: derived statement flips across 73.2% of specification pairs (95% CI 0.725–0.738); modal claim has 41.1% of space. Evidence fails “filability criterion” at every plausible conformity-assessment tolerance. Standardising the most influential choice, evaluation metric, leaves flip rate 59.4%. Removing circuit size from claim entirely and holding it fixed leaves flip rate 27.1% (95% CI 0.255–0.286), still above pre-registered threshold. Circuits structurally near-disjoint: median pairwise Jaccard overlap 4%; functionally uncorrelated: Cohen’s kappa 0.015. Claim: filings differ more than mechanisms throughout circuit-size range.

Intro/reg framing: audit usefulness requires compatible conclusions; circuit-level filing valuable only if second analyst same system/tool would file compatible statement. EU AI Act refs Annex IV 2(b), 2(e), Art 86(1), amended by Reg. 2026/1744. Contributions: pre-registered multiverse over “seven” axes, but formal spec s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g) has eight; deterministic map to Annex IV statements; filability π*≥1−α.

Internal issues: seven-vs-eight axes; Part 5 “binnings differing by factor four” range 0.70–0.77 conflicts with threshold ×0.5 to ×2 range 0.7232–0.7448; H3 summaries say separated distributions though fixed-size H3 was not; §7.4 fixed-size layer-band F=0.2706 conflicts with earlier fixed-size flips 0.2746; Part 12 says null degenerate “above 1,000” though table includes 1,000; says instability entirely below 2,000 though discovered F at 2,000 is 0.5714; Part 15 says Pythia replication has identical axes except seeds 3 not 5 and 924 cells, but realised grid was 1,320 cells with 5 seeds, so analogous 3-seed grid would be 792 unless using failed seventh objective. Part 17 claims every numeric token checked/generated and headline verification 36/36, conflicting with earlier numeric/report inconsistencies.

Key results: GPT-2 small IOI. Realised grid: 6 objectives after one of 7 fails; 1,320 cells; 15,840 specs; 7,561 kept; discard 52.3%. Main overseer/MEDIUM: F=0.7316 CI [0.7247,0.7380], π*=0.4109. Mean Jaccard 0.1396; 3,218 circuits. H4 gap 0.3344. Largest single-axis reduction metric: F to 0.5939 CI [0.5803,0.6063]. Reproducibility: prereg tag, one environment, archive 22/22 files identical, 343 tests.
